06/ 07.11.2025.
Heard, learned counsel for the parties.

1. The instant Cont. Case (Civil) has been filed for non-compliance of the order passed by this Court on 15.04.2025 in WP(C) No.900 of 2025 in which specific direction was given to Respondent No.2- to dispose of the representation and the issue of settlement of account of the petitioner within a period of three months of the order.
2. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the said order has been complied with in breach by passing a belated order dated 08.10.2025.

The non-compliance is on two counts:
Firstly delay in passing the order which has been passed only after the contempt proceeding was initiated and notice was served.
The authority concerned sprang into action and passed the belated reasoned order beyond the period of three months.

Secondly, this Court had taken note of the earlier Police case being Hazaribagh Sadar Muffasil P.S. Case No.22 of 2015 which was lodged under Sections 406 / 409/ 419/
420 and 120B IPC against the petitioner for non-supply of Custom Milled Rice to the FCI and thereby causing embezzlement of Rs.1,71,22,850/- In this case, no material could be shown with regard to embezzlement by the petitioner and consequently,

sentences.text: Final Form No.303 of 2020 was submitted and accepted and the matter was finally dropped.
Despite this, now under the garb of disposing of the representation, a further demand of Rs.65 Lakhs and odd have been raised against the petitioner.

3. It is contended that instant reason order has been passed without hearing the petitioner, which is the corner stone of the principles to be followed by any administrative authority exercising quasi-judicial power.
4. Further, unless the issues raised by way of representation were responded and answered, the order cannot be said to be in conformity and in compliance to the order passed by this Court.

5. Learned counsel for the Opp. Party has submitted that by Speed Post, letters were issued by the contemnor to the petitioner on 25.07.2025 and also on 31.07.2025 to come before the Opp. Party- Managing Director for reconciliation and settlement of the account.
But despite this, the petitioner did not appear and consequently, the authority was constrained to pass order ex-parte.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties, it appears that for one reason or the other, the reasoned order has been passed without hearing the petitioner, which is ex facie violation of the principles of natural justice.
Therefore the reasoned order is not sustainable and is accordingly set aside.

7. Consequently, the petitioner is directed to appear before the Opp.
Party on 18.11.2025 at 10:30 a.m. along-with a fresh representation enclosing therewith all the relevant documents of claim of accounts.
8. After hearing the petitioner and on the representation, a point-wise reasoned order will be passed within four weeks (since 18.11.2025).
List this case on 07.01.2026.

(Gautam Kumar Choudhary, J.) Sandeep/-
Uploade 10.11.2025.
